bib.title: From Recognition to Cognition: Visual Commonsense Reasoning

read.skipped: Reference list and attention-heatmap figure text (Figs 14-18) skimmed only.

question: Can vision systems answer commonsense questions about images and justify the answer, beyond recognition-level understanding?
hypothesis: Cognition-level visual reasoning is easy for humans but hard for current VQA models; a layered grounding-contextualization-reasoning model narrows but does not close the gap.
contributions: Formalize the Visual Commonsense Reasoning task
Present VCR, a large-scale multiple-choice QA dataset
Adversarial Matching, an algorithm for robust multiple-choice dataset creation
R2C model that mimics layered inference from recognition to cognition and sets baselines

method.summary: VCR pairs movie-scene images with crowd-written questions, answers and rationales, turned into 4-way multiple choice by Adversarial Matching (max-weight bipartite matching using BERT relevance and ESIM+ELMo similarity scores). R2C grounds text to image regions with a BiLSTM, contextualizes with attention, and reasons with a second BiLSTM over frozen BERT features and ResNet50 object features.
method.task: Visual commonsense reasoning: multiple-choice QA (Q->A), answer justification (QA->R), and staged Q->AR

datasets.name: VCR
datasets.size: 290k QA problems over 110k movie scenes; train 212,923 / val 26,534 / test 25,263 questions; 80,418 / 9,929 / 9,557 images; 1,945 / 244 / 189 movies
datasets.split: 11 folds split by movie; two folds held out for val and test (one more fold held blind for later evaluation, not counted in Table 3)
datasets.source: LSMDC (46k images in train) and Fandango MovieClips YouTube (33k images in train); Mechanical Turk annotation Aug-Oct 2018; 4 answers and 4 rationales per question
datasets.preprocessing: Shot detection at 1 fps with HSV mean difference 30 pixels; Mask-RCNN X-101-64x4d-FPN threshold 0.7 on middle frame; at least three high-confidence tags; interestingness filter; person tags replaced by gender-neutral names and object tags by class names for text models

datasets.name: SNLI + MultiNLI + back-translated SNLI
datasets.split: SNLI val held out for early stopping
datasets.source: Used to train the similarity model ESIM+ELMo; paraphrases made by En->De->En with Nematus, labelled entailment; random SNLI pairs as extra neutral

datasets.name: TVQA, MovieQA, PororoQA, TGIFQA
datasets.split: PororoQA split by movie 20% val; TGIFQA re-split by GIF 20% val
datasets.preprocessing: TVQA subtitles prepended with separator, trimmed above 128 tokens

models.name: R2C
models.architecture: BiLSTM grounding, bilinear attention contextualization, 2-layer BiLSTM reasoning, MLP scorer over max-pooled features
models.init_from: ResNet50 ImageNet-pretrained (first three blocks frozen); BERT-Base frozen second-to-last layer features, BERT first fine-tuned 1 epoch on VCR text (MLM + NSP)
models.layers: grounding BiLSTM 1 layer; reasoning BiLSTM 2 layers
models.hidden: 256 per LSTM direction; image projection 2176->512; final projection 1024

other.aux_loss: object label prediction from 2048-d ResNet features to prevent drift
other.objects: only objects mentioned in query/responses, plus whole image as an object

models.name: RevisitedVQA, BottomUpTopDown, MLB, MUTAN
models.architecture: VQA models with ResNet50 and GloVe, responses encoded by GRU

models.name: P_rel (BERT-Base)
models.architecture: BERT-Base two-way classifier for query-response relevance

other.finetune: lr 2e-5, Adam, batch 32, 3 epochs; fine-tuned on the other folds; true response with probability 25% else random remapped response

training.objective: multi-class cross entropy over the 4 responses; separate models for Q->A and QA->R
training.lr_schedule: halve when validation accuracy does not increase for two epochs in a row
training.dropout: recurrent dropout on LSTM input, p=0.3
training.regularisation: gradient clipping to L2 norm 1.0; auxiliary object-label loss

inference.decoding: argmax over 4 choices; staged Q->AR requires correct answer then correct rationale
inference.samples: single run per model; seeds not stated

metrics.name: Accuracy QA->R
metrics.definition: pick correct rationale among 4 given question and correct answer

metrics.name: Accuracy Q->AR
metrics.definition: both answer and rationale correct; chance 6.25%

eval.protocol: Standard train/val/test splits; human performance from 5 Mechanical Turk workers per question on 200 test questions, majority vote, different workers for rationales

evidence.quote: Each model was trained for 20 epochs, which took roughly 20 hours over 3 NVIDIA Titan X GPUs.
We chose λ = 0.1 for Q →A and λ = 0.01 for QA →R.

limits: Authors say test accuracy is far from human 85%, so the task is unsolved
BERT is frozen in R2C; authors note fine-tuning end to end would likely raise results (footnote 28)
Language priors remain in QA->R: BERT gets 64.1% val on rationale choice without the image, attributed to the similarity penalty making distractors distinct
Remapped detection tags can yield ungrammatical distractors like 'person1 is kissing person1'
Dataset is biased against women and minorities (movie data); authors recommend not deploying VCR-trained models
Only one model run per entry; seeds and variance not reported; human score from 200 test questions
Superseded: leaderboard results and later models are far above R2C

terms.definition: recycle each correct answer exactly three times as a negative for other questions, chosen by max-weight bipartite matching on log P_rel(q_i,r_j) + lambda log(1 - P_sim(r_i,r_j))
staged holistic task where both the chosen answer and chosen rationale must be correct; chance 6.25%

lineage.note: Text representation in R2C, relevance model P_rel, and strong text-only baseline
Adversarial Matching is contrasted with Adversarial Filtering, which used machine-generated wrong answers

lineage.work: ESIM (Chen et al.) with ELMo (Peters et al.)

lineage.note: VQA models RevisitedVQA, BottomUpTopDown, MLB, MUTAN used as baselines
Object detection and segmentation for tags
